series_items.subject: [PATCH 1/5] mm/mempolicy: add mempolicy_create()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new function, mempolicy_create(), which creates and validates a memory policy without installing it into the current task's policy. The function takes mode, flags, and nodes as arguments, allocates a new policy, constrains it to the task's cpuset, and returns the policy or an error pointer on failure. This patch also exports the symbol for use in guest_memfd integration with KVM.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 2/5] mm/mempolicy: add mpol_set_shared_policy_range()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new function mpol_set_shared_policy_range() that allows installing an already-built memory policy over an arbitrary page range without requiring a VMA. The existing mpol_set_shared_policy() function is reimplemented as a thin wrapper to derive the range from the VMA, allowing both functions to share a single underlying path. This change addresses limitations in the current implementation that make it unusable for binding entire backing inodes from in-kernel code.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 3/5] KVM: guest_memfd: bind backing memory to a NUMA node at creation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new flag called GUEST_MEMFD_FLAG_BIND_NODE to the KVM guest memory file descriptor (memfd) feature. When this flag is set, the backing memory for the guest is bound to a specific NUMA node at creation time, rather than being allocated through a shared mempolicy that can be modified later. This change requires CONFIG_NUMA to be enabled and only allows binding to nodes within the calling task's cpuset. The policy is fixed for the life of the fd and cannot be rebound on later cpuset changes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 4/5] selftests: KVM: guest_memfd: let the gmem_test() harness bind a node
series_items.patch_summary: This patch extends the create_guest_memfd() function to accept a node argument, allowing the gmem_test() harness to bind a node when creating a guest memory file descriptor. The BIND_NODE flag is used to determine whether the node argument should be ignored or used for binding. This change enables testing of GUEST_MEMFD_FLAG_BIND_NODE functionality.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 5/5] selftests: KVM: guest_memfd: test GUEST_MEMFD_FLAG_BIND_NODE
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds tests for the GUEST_MEMFD_FLAG_BIND_NODE flag in KVM's guest_memfd feature. The tests cover various scenarios, including single and multi-node systems, invalid arguments, and edge cases such as non-zero padding and out-of-range node numbers. The tests ensure that the BIND_NODE flag behaves correctly when used with other flags and when faults occur on remote nodes.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series introduces a new flag, GUEST_MEMFD_FLAG_BIND_NODE, to the KVM guest memory file descriptor (memfd) API. When set, this flag binds the backing memory of the memfd to a specific NUMA node, ensuring that all allocated folios are placed on that node. This is done by creating an MPOL_BIND policy for the requested node and installing it over the whole inode. The patch series includes preparatory work in the mm/mempolicy code, as well as selftest harness support and testing. The approach taken is to bind each fd to a single host node, rather than allowing interleaving across multiple nodes, which would defeat guest NUMA balancing decisions.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 1/2] mm/mempolicy: use SRCU for the weighted interleave state
series_items.patch_summary: This patch replaces the current implementation of weighted interleave state management in the Linux kernel's memory policy module with a new approach using SRCU (Schedulable RCU) to pin the global iw_table object and use it in-place. This change allows for more efficient handling of concurrent updates to the weights, reducing the need for synchronization and improving performance. The patch also introduces a new mechanism for retiring the weighted interleave state, which involves calling SRCU for sleeping readers and kfree_rcu for reference-less ones. The changes were tested with various configurations and tools, including KASAN, PROVE_LOCKING, and DEBUG_OBJECTS_RCU_HEAD.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 2/2] mm/mempolicy: stop copying the nodemask in the interleave paths
series_items.patch_summary: This patch removes the unnecessary copying of a nodemask in interleave node selectors, which reduces memory usage and improves performance. The original copy was done to ensure consistency between the node count and the walk, but this is no longer necessary as bounds checking can be used instead. If an empty nodelist or weight is detected, the patch falls back to using numa_node_id(). This change affects several functions in the mm/mempolicy.c file, including weighted_interleave_nid() and interleave_nid(), which are used for allocating pages under a specific memory policy.

review_comments.author: Rakie Kim
review_comments.summary:
The reviewer pointed out that the patch's removal of read_once_policy_nodemask() may cause a potential issue in alloc_pages_bulk_weighted_interleave(), where the function derives per-node counts from a weight total summed over the mask, and a changing mask can make them exceed the request.

Reviewer Rakie Kim agreed that resolving the sleeping-allocation problem using SRCU is a better approach than patching the allocation site and removing copies from the fault path.

Reviewer Rakie Kim noted that after removing the nodemask copy, the loop bound in alloc_pages_bulk_weighted_interleave() no longer matches the actual mask being walked, which can cause the walk to stop short of the intended pages. They suggested counting nodes in the loop that sums weights, as done in weighted_interleave_nid(), to fix this issue.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/3] fs: stamp the current time for a stale delegated ctime update
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the Linux kernel's inode_set_ctime_deleg function, which drops updates that do not advance the ctime when they are actually valid and should be applied. The patch adds logic to stamp the current time for stale delegated ctime updates, ensuring that the ctime never moves backwards. This fix addresses an issue introduced by a previous patch (3952f1cbcbc4) and is assisted by LLM. The changes affect the fs/inode.c file and are part of a larger series of patches.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/3] nfsd: accept a backdated timestamp from a delegation holder
series_items.patch_summary: This patch allows the NFS server to accept a backdated timestamp from a delegation holder, which was previously ignored if it moved backwards in time. The client can report file times at every delegation return, and the server will update them accordingly. If an mtime moves backwards, the ctime is set to the current time. The patch also fixes issues with caching and attribute updates when using delegations.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/3] nfsd: compare CB_GETATTR times against the inode
series_items.patch_summary: This patch updates the NFS server to compare client-reported timestamps in CB_GETATTR requests against the current timestamp of the inode, rather than stale values stored in the delegation. This change prevents clients from reporting outdated timestamps and ensures that file metadata is accurately updated. The patch also removes unnecessary fields from the delegation structure and fixes a bug related to SETATTR updates for delegated timestamps.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses an issue where applications cannot set backdated timestamps on files after writing them, due to strict attribute delegation rules in NFS. The solution is to modify the server-side handling of ctime updates, allowing it to accept these backdated mtime updates. This is achieved by changing how the ctime is handled and comparing against the inode instead of grant-time snapshots.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 01/15] NFSD: cap the number of listeners accepted in listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch limits the number of listeners accepted in the listener_set function to prevent a userland request from spinning indefinitely due to excessive nesting loops under sv_lock. The limit is set at 1024, which is considered far above any realistic configuration. The patch introduces a new constant NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX and adds a check in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners() to reject requests with more than this number of listeners. This prevents potential deadlocks and ensures the system remains responsive.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 02/15] NFSD: validate transport name in listener_set before serv creation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a validation check for the transport name in the listener_set netlink command before creating a service. The code checks if the provided transport name is one of 'tcp', 'udp', or 'rdma' and rejects any other names. This prevents an arbitrary string from reaching the svc_xprt_create_from_sa function, which can trigger a request_module upcall under nfsd_mutex. The check is done in the nfsd_nl_validate_listeners function before taking the nfsd_mutex lock.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 03/15] SUNRPC: keep the first error in svc_register()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the svc_register() function in the SUNRPC module to keep track of the first error encountered during RPC program registration, rather than overwriting it with subsequent errors.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 04/15] SUNRPC: bound the local rpcbind client timeout to 1s
series_items.patch_summary: This patch limits the timeout for local rpcbind client connections to 1 second. The current default timeouts of 10 seconds for AF_LOCAL and 60 seconds for loopback TCP fallback can cause stalls in NFS server operations, leading to hung-task watchdog warnings. By setting a shorter timeout, the patch reduces the duration of these stalls, but does not eliminate them entirely. A more comprehensive solution would be to make the registration process asynchronous.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 05/15] NFSD: report listener creation failures through extack
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) code to report listener creation failures through extack, a mechanism for returning detailed error messages from kernel space to userland. When a listener creation fails, the patch records the attribute and transport name of the failing entry and reports both after the loop. This allows userland to receive more informative error messages when creating listeners, which can help with debugging and troubleshooting.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 06/15] SUNRPC: report local rpcbind calls that get no answer
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the SUNRPC code to report local rpcbind calls that fail without an answer, distinguishing between different types of failures such as transport errors and soft timeouts. It introduces a new counter in the svc_serv structure to track the number of unanswered rpcbind calls, which will be used by later patches to adjust their behavior accordingly.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 07/15] SUNRPC: stop svc_register() once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the svc_register() function in the SUNRPC module to stop registering programs when rpcbind does not respond. The original implementation would continue trying to register other programs even if one program's call timed out, resulting in unnecessary delays. This change improves performance by breaking out of the loop as soon as a program fails to respond.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 08/15] SUNRPC: stop the svc_unregister() sweep once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the svc_unregister() function to stop sweeping for stale rpcbind entries once it receives no answer from rpcbind. This is done by returning immediately when __svc_unregister() returns -EIO, indicating that rpcbind did not respond. The goal of this change is to reduce the number of timeouts and improve performance in scenarios where a local rpcbind never replies.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 09/15] SUNRPC: stop unregistering listeners once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the SUNRPC code to stop unregistering listeners once rpcbind stops answering. The original behavior caused a local rpcbind timeout for each listener, which could lead to multiple timeouts and failures during teardown. To fix this, the patch introduces a new function `svc_xprt_clear_rpcb_unreg` that clears the `XPT_RPCB_UNREG` flag on remaining transports when rpcbind stops answering. This change improves the robustness of the SUNRPC code by reducing the number of timeouts and potential failures during teardown.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 10/15] NFSD: stop registering with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a performance issue in the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) component of the Linux kernel. When attempting to set up listeners, the code would register each listener individually with rpcbind, which could lead to a high number of timeouts and potentially cause the system to hang. The patch introduces a check for rpcbind failures before creating new listeners, and if a failure is detected, it skips registering with rpcbind for subsequent listeners. This approach reduces the likelihood of timeouts and prevents the system from becoming unresponsive.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 11/15] SUNRPC: check rpc_sockaddr2uaddr() for failure when registering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the SUNRPC code by checking if rpc_sockaddr2uaddr() returns NULL due to memory allocation failure, and returning -ENOMEM instead of proceeding with potentially invalid operations. This ensures that the universal address is properly checked for validity before being used. The fix addresses an issue introduced by a previous commit that removed duplicate universal address generation.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 12/15] selftests/nfsd: exercise listener_set request validation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds regression tests for the NFSD_CMD_LISTENER_SET checks in the nfsd_netlink_listener code. The tests cover various invalid listener_set requests, including bad transport names, missing addresses, and malformed entries. The tests use kselftest_harness.h to run in their own network namespace and mount namespace, and they do not create any services or register with rpcbind. The patch also updates the MAINTAINERS file and adds a new directory for nfsd selftests.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 13/15] selftests/nfsd: add a per-netns rpcbind stub and the listener round-trips
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a per-netns rpcbind stub to the selftests/nfsd module, allowing it to serve rpcbind from within each network namespace. The stub is used to register listeners and handle round-trips for various tests, including TCP, UDP, multiple listeners, and IPv6. The patch also includes test cases that cover create, add, and remove paths, as well as LISTENER_GET round trips. By serving rpcbind from within the namespace, the patch resolves issues with listener registration timeouts and ensures proper cleanup of network namespaces.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 14/15] selftests/nfsd: check that listener_set asks rpcbind once
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds self-tests to the NFS daemon (nfsd) to ensure that listener_set requests only ask rpcbind once, even if it stops answering. The tests cover various scenarios, including stopping a listener after failure, silent set completion, and bounded version sets. A new function, version_set_only(), is introduced to enable exactly one NFS version in a network namespace. The patch also includes changes to the nfsd_netlink_listener.c file to implement these self-tests.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 15/15] selftests/nfsd: check that listener removal asks rpcbind once
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a new test case to the NFS daemon selftest suite. The test checks that when a listener is removed, rpcbind is only asked once to unregister it, rather than once for each listener removed. This ensures that removing multiple listeners does not result in multiple timeouts due to repeated requests to rpcbind.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series hardens the netlink listener set interface in the NFS daemon and SunRPC code. It addresses issues such as incorrect error handling, listener registration problems, and potential hangs. The patches fix various bugs, including a case where a failed registration would leave behind orphaned entries in rpcbind. They also improve test coverage and add new tests to ensure correct behavior. The changes aim to make the netlink listener set interface more robust and reliable.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the performance of the nested loop in nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit(), which can spin in atomic context for a long time when dealing with large listener lists. The author explained that this is due to an O(N * M) complexity, where N is the requested count and M is the existing count, and proposed rejecting requests with more than NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX (1024) entries to prevent this issue.
review_comments.raw_body:
nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() matches each requested listener against the
existing set. The nested loop that does this is O(N * M), where N is the
requested count and M is the existing count. The loop runs under sv_lock
with bottom halves disabled. A userland request with a very large listener
list can therefore spin in atomic context for a long time.

Reject a request that carries more than NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX (1024)
entries. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), before the code
takes any lock. The limit is far above any realistic configuration.

This patch does not cap M. Only the message size bounded N; real sockets
bound M. A listener_set result set is the requested set, so that path also
holds M at the cap, but __write_ports_addxprt() adds two listeners per call
and removes none, so repeated calls can push M past it. The worst case
under sv_lock is therefore 1024 * M, plus 1024 nla_parse_nested() calls.
Both interfaces require CAP_NET_ADMIN.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the nfsd_mutex being held for an extended period during listener teardown and rebuild, explaining that it is necessary to prevent a TASK_KILLABLE usermode helper upcall from running under nfsd_mutex. The check for supported transport classes has been moved to before taking the mutex, and the rejection now names the offending attribute through extack.
sentiment_signals: neutral explanation with no clear resolution signal
review_comments.raw_body:
nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() holds nfsd_mutex for the whole listener
teardown and rebuild. The code checks NFSD_A_SOCK_TRANSPORT_NAME for
presence only, and not for content. An arbitrary name therefore reaches
svc_xprt_create_from_sa(). There, a name that matches no registered class
calls request_module("svc%s", name). That call is a TASK_KILLABLE usermode
helper upcall, and it runs under nfsd_mutex.

Check the name against the classes that NFSD can create: tcp, udp and
rdma. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), which runs before
the code takes nfsd_mutex. The rejection names the offending attribute
through extack, since -EPROTONOSUPPORT on its own does not say which
entry carried the bad name.

This narrows the upcall. It does not remove it. NFSD accepts "rdma"
without a condition, so on a kernel that does not build svcrdma the name
still reaches request_module("svcrdma") under nfsd_mutex. That is
necessary for the modular case, where the autoload is legitimate.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton (author)
review_comments.summary: The author addressed a concern about the kernel's local rpcbind client causing stalls due to synchronous registration calls. They acknowledged that the current fix shortens the stall but does not remove it, and explained that the real solution is to make the registration asynchronous.
review_comments.raw_body:
The kernel's local rpcbind client uses the transport defaults: a 10s major
timeout for AF_LOCAL, and 60s for the loopback TCP fallback.
xprt_calc_majortimeo() returns to_initval when to_increment is 0.

Those calls are synchronous, and they run under nfsd_mutex. One operation
makes several of them. rpcb_create_local() tries up to three client
creations, and svc_register() sends one call for each program and version.
A local rpcbind that accepts the connection but never replies stalls every
one of these calls. The accumulated hold is long enough to trip the
hung-task watchdog on other NFSD netlink operations. The holder itself
waits killably and escapes the watchdog:

  INFO: task hung in nfsd_nl_cache_flush_doit

The local rpcbind is on loopback or on an AF_LOCAL socket, and it answers
in microseconds. Bound its client to one attempt of 1s.

This shortens the stall. It does not remove the stall, and it is not free.
Registration stays synchronous and stays fatal. An rpcb_create_local()
failure aborts nfsd_create_serv() through svc_bind(), and an
svc_register() failure makes svc_setup_socket() fail. An rpcbind that is
merely slow to be scheduled can therefore now fail server startup, where
it succeeded before. The real fix is to make the registration
asynchronous.

patches_reviewed.subject: Re: [PATCH v2] fs/locks: filter OFD locks from /proc/locks for foreign pid namespaces
patches_reviewed.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue where /proc/locks was not correctly filtering out Open File Descriptor (OFD) locks from foreign process ID namespaces. The problem arose because these locks are visible to the system but not shown in /proc/locks, leading to inconsistent results and potential confusion. The patch considers alternative approaches, including showing all locks with a negative pid for those acquired in foreign namespaces.

review_comments.author: Tao Cui
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer questioned the correctness of hiding OFD locks from /proc/locks and suggested showing all locks instead, reporting foreign pid namespaces as negative values or using a similar approach to remote locks.

Reviewer noted that folding the check into locks_translate_pid() would cause F_GETLK/F_OFD_GETLK to report a conflicting OFD lock with l_pid = 0 instead of -1, as documented by fcntl(2), and expressed hesitation about this change.

Reviewer noted that hiding OFD locks from /proc/locks may be confusing and suggested anonymizing the owner instead, citing precedent from fdinfo and potential debugging benefits.
review_comments.raw_body:
Hi, Jeff

\u5728 2026/9/2 21:03, Jeff Layton \u5199\u9053:

---

Good point. I did consider that.  My hesitation with folding it into
locks_translate_pid() is that posix_lock_to_flock() also uses it, so
F_GETLK/F_OFD_GETLK would then report a conflicting OFD lock with
l_pid = 0 instead of the -1 that fcntl(2) documents for OFD locks.
That's why I kept the check in locks_show(), where it only affects
the /proc/locks view.

That distinction isn't introduced by this patch, though, since it
already exists for POSIX locks: since the 4.9 pid namespace filter, a
foreign-namespace POSIX lock that blocks F_GETLK is reported there
with l_pid = 0 while /proc/locks hides it.  v2 just gives OFD locks
the same treatment.

---

That's a reasonable alternative - anonymizing the owner instead of
hiding the lock does have precedent (fdinfo follows that model), and I
can see the debugging benefit of always showing locks that may block
acquisition.  I went with hiding because it preserves the /proc/locks
visibility semantics introduced in 4.9 by making OFD locks consistent
with POSIX locks.  With only the pid anonymized, the output would
still disclose which files are locked and the locked byte ranges of
tasks outside the reader's pid namespace.

If the consensus is that /proc/locks should show all locks with an
anonymized pid instead, I'm happy to rework the patch in that
direction.

Thanks,
Tao

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch optimizes memory control group (memcg) statistics by skipping non-hierarchical memcg-wide stats on the default hierarchy, reducing flush costs and improving performance. The optimization is based on the observation that only legacy memory.stat and memory.numa_stat readers access these stats, which are not used on the default hierarchy. By skipping these stats, the patch reduces cacheline accesses and improves flush function performance by 2.2%. The change also includes a mechanism to handle cases where a controller is moved from the default hierarchy to the legacy v1 hierarchy at runtime.

review_comments.author: Usama Arif
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Usama Arif reported that on GPU hosts during AI-training checkpointing, they experienced significant latency spikes and workload timeouts due to unmovable memory and order-0 allocations falling back to MIGRATE_MOVABLE free lists, leading to contaminated movable pageblocks with unmovable pages that caused sustained compaction activity.
review_comments.raw_body:
The issue that finally pushed us toward 2 MiB pageblocks occurred on
GPU hosts during AI-training checkpointing. We observed significant
latency spikes and workload timeouts.

These hosts had substantial unmovable memory, and order-0 allocations
from TCP paths repeatedly fell back to MIGRATE_MOVABLE free lists.
With 512 MiB pageblocks, try_to_claim_block() often could not meet
the half-pageblock threshold, so allocation fell through to stealing
individual pages.

This contaminated very large movable pageblocks with unmovable pages.
Compaction then repeatedly scanned those pageblocks but could not
evacuate the unmovable allocations. We observed sustained compaction
activity during the latency spikes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 8/8] memcg: simplify v1 event ratelimiting
series_items.patch_summary: This patch simplifies the v1 event ratelimiting in the Linux kernel's memory control group (memcg) by collapsing multiple periodic events into a single counter. The target enum, per-cpu target array, and switch in memcg1_event_ratelimit() are all reduced to a single threshold counter. This change also removes the need for a node ID in memcg1_check_events(), allowing it to drop its nid argument and related struct changes. The patch aims to improve code simplicity and reduce complexity by eliminating unnecessary variables and logic.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series removes the deprecated v1 soft limit in memory cgroups, which has been inert since v6.12 and covered by newer features like memory.low and memory.min. The removal includes deleting various machinery such as reclaim pass, direct reclaim, tracepoints, per-node rbtree, and event ratelimiting.

review_comments.author: Andrew Morton
review_comments.summary: Confirmed that v2 made no changes to mm.git and updated mm-unstable.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Wed,  2 Sep 2026 10:43:03 -0700 Shakeel Butt <shakeel.butt@linux.dev> wrote:

> The v1 soft limit was deprecated in v6.12 by commit 569c4f62d84a ("memcg:
> initiate deprecation of v1 soft limit") and nobody has reported depending
> on it in the ~21 months since. memory.low and memory.min in v2 have
> covered the same ground for far longer.
> 
> The knob has since been made inert by "memcg: make the v1 soft limit knob
> inert", already queued in mm-hotfixes as a backportable fix for a syzbot
> report [1]. Nothing can enter the soft limit rbtree anymore, so this
> series just deletes the machinery that is now dead: the reclaim pass in
> kswapd and direct reclaim, mem_cgroup_shrink_node() and its tracepoints,
> the per-node rbtree, lru_gen_soft_reclaim() and the MEMCG_LRU_HEAD op, the
> per-node tree fields, mem_cgroup->soft_limit, and finally the v1 event
> ratelimiting which is now down to a single target.
> 
> memory.soft_limit_in_bytes itself is untouched: writes stay ignored and
> reads keep returning the maximum value.

Thanks, I updated mm-unstable.

> Changes since v1 [2]:

>   already queued in mm-hotfixes, making this an 8-patch series.
> - Collected the acks and review tags. No code changes.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2] selftests: cover kernfs dentry revalidation

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2] selftests: cover kernfs dentry revalidation

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch adds tests to the Linux kernel selftest suite to cover kernfs dentry revalidation. The existing tests only checked two xattr calls, but did not verify the dentry cache. This patch introduces new tests that simulate kernel actions on kernfs nodes without VFS calls, and checks how the dentry cache is updated accordingly. The tests cover various scenarios such as adding and removing files in child cgroups, renaming network interfaces, sysfs mounted in a new network namespace, concurrent mkdir and rmdir operations, and open across removal. Additionally, it ensures that walking dentries that are already cached does not drop them. This patch aims to prevent broken backstops by ensuring the tests catch any issues with kernfs dentry revalidation.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] mm/mlock: use the IRQ-safe accessor for NR_MLOCK in __munlock_folio()

version_history.subject: [PATCH] mm/mlock: use the IRQ-safe accessor for NR_MLOCK in __munlock_folio()

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the Linux kernel's memory locking mechanism where NR_MLOCK, a counter of locked pages, could be overstated due to concurrent access from interrupt context and user space. The issue arises when a folio is munlocked while still pinned by a bio completion handler. To fix this, the patch uses an IRQ-safe accessor for NR_MLOCK in __munlock_folio(), specifically zone_stat_mod_folio(). This ensures that the counter update is atomic and accurate, preventing permanent overstatement of locked pages in /proc/meminfo.

review_comments.author: Hugh Dickins
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Hugh Dickins noted that the rare fallback case where PG_mlocked is cleared late can occur at interrupt time, and therefore the shortcut in __munlock_folio() should not be taken.

Reviewer Hugh Dickins noted that the patch does not address a separate issue related to offlining a CPU, which was reported by syzbot and resulted in a WARNING. He suggested adding Reported-by and Closes tags to acknowledge the report and indicate that it is fixed by this patch.
review_comments.raw_body:
I'm hardly ashamed to admit that I've not tried to digest
that paragraph. You're writing about the rare fallback cases when
PG_mlocked is cleared late, and unevictable_pgs_cleared incremented to
notify us of that defect: yes, I accept that might happen at interrupt
time, and so we ought not to take the __shortcut in __munlock_folio()
which you fix  below.

---

Acked-by: Hugh Dickins <hughd@google.com>

But I do think you (or Andrew :-) should include

Reported-by: syzbot+cd2073ee6d958a8d0fcd@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/6a931c5a.08e933ee.dbf97.0093.GAE@google.com/

That was indeed reporting a different way to get a WARNING from this,
when offlining a CPU: but it should be acknowledged for bringing you
here, and we should tell syzbot it's fixed by this.

I've been trying to work out whether you're going to come back in a
day or two, changing the __count_vm_events() too: and had raised in
that thread the question of why lru_add_drain()'s __count_vm_events
were not also reported by syzbot; but now I can see
 * vm counters are allowed to be racy. Use raw_cpu_ops to avoid the
 * local_irq_disable overhead.
and realize that they're not a problem; so this looks complete, we
shouldn't need local_lock()ing in mlock_drain_remote() after all.

Thanks,
Hugh
